PagerDuty: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident INC-395123-AUTOSCALE triggered for eng-oncall — reason: inference queue depth > 4.5k (sustained 6m)
OpsBot: Automatic page sent to rotation: @alex.r :bell: (strategy: primary)
Alex R: ack — I'm on it. Who's got autoscaler/controller logs?
Meera K: pulling controller + nodepool logs now (last 20m).
PagerDuty: Incident details: priority P1, service=inference-producer-hosted. Symptoms: long queuing, spike in 5xx and OOMs on sidecars.
Meera K: quick snapshot: queue ~4800, median latency 18s for short gen, 5xx at 4.1% on premium endpoints.
Jordan T: looking at controller logs — autoscaler attempted scale but hit provider error repeatedly. snippet:
```
E030 03:12:05 scaler.go:412] scale failed: provider error: googleapi: Error 403: accessNotConfigured Google Cloud API has not been used in project before or it is disabled., accessNotConfigured
I030 03:12:06 scaler.go:420] reconcile loop retrying in 30s
```
Alex R: accessNotConfigured? weird. Did someone change SA permissions or disable compute api?
Jordan T: I see an IAM denier in cloud audit logs at 03:07 from service-account: `autoscaler@prod` — role lacked compute.instances.create. Possibly an automated policy removal from last patch.
Meera K: impact summary: new nodes not coming up; current pods hitting memory pressure and OOMing; autoscaler giving up after retries -> backlog grows.
Alex R: mitigation options: 1) manually scale nodepool via infra team (needs elevated perms), 2) fallback traffic to quantized smaller model variant (redwood-lite-q), 3) throttling or 429s for non-SLA tiers, 4) evict non-critical batch jobs using console.
PagerDuty: Escalate to eng-sre in 8m if unacknowledged.
Jordan T: I'm going to open a quick infra support SR for permissions and ping cloud admin. Sam, can you pause noisy batch jobs?
Sam P: paused batch job group job-bulk-analytics-2 (owner notified) — reclaimed ~8 GPUs worth of capacity from ephemeral pool.
Meera K: applying a canary route to shift 30% traffic to redwood-lite-q. Calling router API: POST /router/v1/traffic -> {service: inference-producer, variant: redwood-lite-q, weight: 30}%
OpsBot: Routing request initiated by Meera K.
Alex R: while routing shifts, Jordan — can you attempt manual nodepool scale using cloud CLI under your account? If IAM denies, we know it's SA permission.
Jordan T: trying: `gcloud container node-pools resize prod-pool --num-nodes=20 --zone=us-central1-a` -> response: Operation denied: caller lacks permission compute.instances.create.
Meera K: routing in place. After shift, pod CPU/GPU load reduced ~26%. Queue now ~3000 and trending down.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Alex R at 3951234589
Jordan T: cloud admin replied — a recent IAM housekeeping job mistakenly removed compute.instanceAdmin role from autoscaler service account. They've restored it and are propagating.
Meera K: good. Observability: 5xx down to 1.1% and latency median 10s. Queue dropping to ~1200 in 6m.
Alex R: once permissions propagate, autoscaler should pick up. Jordan, can you watch controller reconcile logs and post when it scales?
Jordan T: controller logged successful scale at 3951234682 -> desired=18 current=12, scale op started. Pods scheduling now.
Meera K: backlog drained to ~250. Some in-flight requests still slow but decreasing.
Alex R: Start partial rollback of routing to move 15% back to default to normalize outputs.
Meera K: applied rollback 15% -> default now 85% / lite-q 15%. Monitoring for quality regressions.
Sam P: batch jobs remain paused until we confirm stable. Batch owner acknowledged.
PagerDuty: No further escalation required as incident acknowledged and mitigation in flight.
Alex R: post-incident actions: 1) request audit + alert for IAM role changes on autoscaler SA, 2) add autoscaler graceful fallback to smaller variants when scale attempts fail due to quota/perm, 3) add runbook step to prefer routing fallback earlier. Assigning owners.
Meera K: I'll take postmortem (PM-395123) and include timeline, graphs, commands, and follow-ups.
Alex R: handoff to night on-call @jordan.t in 20m. If anything re-fires, escalate to eng-sre channel.
Jordan T: taking handoff — leaving controller log level at debug for 10m and an alert for queue>500 persists. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
OpsBot: Incident thread marked mitigated by Alex R. Last state: healthy, queue drained to <100, autoscaler operational. Postmortem ticket PM-395123 assigned to Meera K.
